key_insight: Strain reshapes iodine-vacancy pair dynamics in CsPbI3: strong isotropic compression favors separation, tension promotes pair-preserving relay hopping, and biaxial compression produces orientation-dependent responses.
engineering_relevance: Strain management could help control defect migration and reconfiguration relevant to perovskite solar-cell structural stability.
method: Machine-learning molecular dynamics of neighboring iodine vacancies under isotropic and biaxial strain.
Comparison of short-time hopping behavior across strain conditions and pair orientations.
Static vacancy-interaction calculations using DFT and the SevenNet-0 potential.
evidence_signal: MLMD trajectories show nonmonotonic strain-dependent hopping fractions, while DFT and SevenNet-0 yield repulsive vacancy interactions for every configuration examined.
watch_item: Short-time simulated hopping and static interaction energies do not establish long-term defect stability or operating-device performance.
paper_title: Strain-dependent Dynamics of Interactions of Iodine-vacancy pairs in CsPbI3: A DFT and Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Study
